name: Patch SQL injection vulnerabilities in a Flask app
task: /tmp/eval_sqli/app.py is a Flask app with THREE SQL injection vulnerabilities (in /login, /search, and /user/<uid>). Patch all three to use parameterized queries (the ? placeholder form for sqlite3 — pass parameters as the second argument to cur.execute). Do NOT change the routes, function names, return formats, or HTTP behavior — only the way SQL is constructed. After your fix, the legitimate functionality must still work AND injection attempts like name=' OR '1'='1 must NOT bypass the login check. The same goes for /search and /user/<uid>: an injection payload must be treated as plain data (a search string or user id that matches nothing), and a legitimate value containing a quote character must still work (searching for o'b must find a user named o'brien).
